provenance_summary: V1-B first expansion wave. Electrospun nanofiber membranes with high surface area and tunable porosity for heavy metal, dye, and particulate removal.

mechanisms.description: Size exclusion filtration: nanofiber membrane pore structure physically blocks particles and macromolecules while allowing water permeation

interaction.text: Physical size exclusion via nanofiber pore structure

why_it_works.text: High rejection rate for particles > pore size

boundary_conditions.text: Use only within the pollutant/material/pH and source context cited for this mechanism.

causal_chain.transferable_principle: Size exclusion filtration: nanofiber membrane pore structure physically blocks particles and macromolecules while allowing water permeation

mechanisms.name: Size exclusion filtration

engineering_constraints.description: Electrospinning parameters: voltage, feed rate, tip-to-collector distance control fiber diameter and membrane porosity

design_translation.idea: Use electrospinning to create nanofiber membranes with controlled fiber diameter and pore size for filtration and adsorption applications
examples: Cellulose nanofiber membrane for heavy metal removal
Polymer nanofiber membrane for dye filtration
design_translation.applicability: Water filtration, heavy metal removal, dye removal, particulate removal

knowledge_gaps: Specific adsorption capacity data not available

narrative.text: Electrospun nanofiber membranes offer high surface area, tunable porosity, and flexibility in material choice. They can be functionalized with specific groups for targeted adsorption.
